    86	/// Read + parse `xl/styles.xml` from the package. Returns
    87	/// `Ok(StyleIndex::default())` if the part doesn't exist (legal in
    88	/// OOXML — a workbook with no custom styles can omit it; the engine
    89	/// just sees an empty index).
    90	pub(crate) fn parse_styles_xml(package: &XlsxPackage) -> Result<StyleIndex, XlsxError> {
    91	    const PART: &str = "xl/styles.xml";
    92	    let content = match package.read_part_string(PART)? {
    93	        Some(c) => c,
    94	        None => return Ok(StyleIndex::default()),
    95	    };
    96	
    97	    let mut reader = Reader::from_str(&content);
    98	    reader.config_mut().trim_text(true);
    99	
   100	    let mut idx = StyleIndex::default();
   101	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
   102	    // Stack of currently-open element names. Used to decide whether
   103	    // an `<xf>` belongs to `<cellXfs>` (the per-cell table we care
   104	    // about) or to `<cellStyleXfs>` (named styles — out of scope).
   105	    let mut element_stack: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   106	
   107	    loop {
   108	        let evt = reader
   109	            .read_event_into(&mut buf)
   110	            .map_err(|e| XlsxError::XmlParse {
   111	                part: PART.to_string(),
   112	                source: e,
   113	            })?;
   114	        match evt {
   115	            Event::Start(e) => {
   116	                let local_name = e.local_name();
   117	                let tag = std::str::from_utf8(local_name.as_ref())
   118	                    .unwrap_or("")
   119	                    .to_string();
   120	                // **W5-D-15.1 (self-audit H-2 root-cause closure):**
   121	                // LibreOffice emits `<xf>...</xf>` (non-self-closing,
   122	                // with `<alignment>` / `<protection>` children) — those
   123	                // come through as `Event::Start`, NOT `Event::Empty`.
   124	                // Without this branch, every cellXf in a LibreOffice
   125	                // file was silently dropped from the index.
   126	                if tag == "xf" && element_stack.last().map(String::as_str) == Some("cellXfs") {
   127	                    idx.cell_xfs.push(parse_xf_attrs(&e));
   128	                }
   129	                element_stack.push(tag);
   130	            }
   131	            Event::Empty(e) => {
   132	                let local_name = e.local_name();
   133	                let tag = std::str::from_utf8(local_name.as_ref()).unwrap_or("");
   134	                match tag {
   135	                    "numFmt" => {
   136	                        if let Some(entry) = parse_numfmt_attrs(&e) {
   137	                            idx.num_fmts.push(entry);
   138	                        }
   139	                    }
   140	                    "xf" if element_stack.last().map(String::as_str) == Some("cellXfs") => {
   141	                        // Only count `<xf>` elements inside `<cellXfs>`,
   142	                        // not `<cellStyleXfs>` (named styles — out of scope).
   143	                        idx.cell_xfs.push(parse_xf_attrs(&e));
   144	                    }
   145	                    _ => {}
   146	                }
   147	            }
   148	            Event::End(_) => {
   149	                element_stack.pop();
   150	            }
   151	            Event::Eof => break,
   152	            _ => {}
   153	        }
   154	        buf.clear();
   155	    }
   156	
   157	    Ok(idx)
   158	}
   159	
   160	fn parse_numfmt_attrs(e: &quick_xml::events::BytesStart) -> Option<NumFmtEntry> {
   161	    let mut num_fmt_id: Option<u32> = None;
   162	    let mut format_code = String::new();
   163	    for attr in e.attributes().with_checks(false).flatten() {
   164	        let key = attr.key.as_ref();
   165	        let val = attr.unescape_value().unwrap_or_default();
   166	        if key == b"numFmtId" {
   167	            num_fmt_id = val.parse::<u32>().ok();
   168	        } else if key == b"formatCode" {
   169	            format_code = val.to_string();
   170	        }
   171	    }
   172	    let id = num_fmt_id?;
   173	    if format_code.is_empty() {
   174	        return None;
   175	    }
   176	    Some(NumFmtEntry {
   177	        num_fmt_id: id,
   178	        format_code,
   179	    })
   180	}
   181	
   182	fn parse_xf_attrs(e: &quick_xml::events::BytesStart) -> CellXf {
   183	    let mut num_fmt_id: u32 = 0;
   184	    // **W5-D-15.1 (self-audit H-2 closure):** the OOXML schema
   185	    // default for `applyNumberFormat` on `<cellXfs>/<xf>` is TRUE
   186	    // when the attribute is absent. LibreOffice-generated files
   187	    // commonly omit the attr but still expect the numFmtId to be
   188	    // applied — verified empirically against
   189	    // `libreoffice_888_example.xlsx` (numFmtId=165 xf with no
   190	    // applyNumberFormat attr → format IS applied per the spec).
   191	    // The prior `false` default silently dropped these on import.
   192	    let mut apply_number_format = true;
   193	    for attr in e.attributes().with_checks(false).flatten() {
   194	        let key = attr.key.as_ref();
   195	        let val = attr.unescape_value().unwrap_or_default();
   196	        if key == b"numFmtId" {
   197	            num_fmt_id = val.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0);
   198	        } else if key == b"applyNumberFormat" {
   199	            // Explicit attr: "1"/"true" → apply; "0"/"false" → don't.
   200	            apply_number_format = val == "1" || val.eq_ignore_ascii_case("true");
   201	        }
   202	    }
   203	    CellXf {
   204	        num_fmt_id,
   205	        apply_number_format,
   206	    }
   207	}

   388	/// Unified post-process pass over the just-written xlsx. Applies all
   389	/// workarounds and roster injections in a single zip walk:
   390	/// - `xl/workbook.xml`: inject `date1904="1"` + `<definedNames>`.
   391	/// - `xl/worksheets/sheet{N}.xml`: per-cell fixes (HIGH-1 / HIGH-6) +
   392	///   `<tableParts>` references for tables anchored to that sheet.
   393	/// - `xl/styles.xml`: inject `<numFmts>` for custom format codes.
   394	/// - `xl/tables/table{N}.xml`: NEW parts for each Quantbook table.
   395	/// - `xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet{N}.xml.rels`: rel entries pointing
   396	///   into the table parts.
   397	/// - `[Content_Types].xml`: `Override` entries for the new table parts.
   398	///
   399	/// **W5-D-14.1** audit HIGH-1 / HIGH-2 / HIGH-6 closure.
   400	/// **W5-D-14.2** audit HIGH-3 / HIGH-4 / HIGH-5 closure.
   401	fn post_process_zip(
   402	    path: &std::path::Path,
   403	    inject_date1904: bool,
   404	    sheet_fixes: &[Vec<CellFix>],
   405	    custom_formats: &[(u32, String)],
   406	    defined_names: &[DefinedNameOut],
   407	    tables: &[TableExport],
   408	    cellxfs_roster: &[FormatId],
   409	) -> Result<(), XlsxError> {
   410	    use std::io::{Read, Write};
   411	
   412	    // Pre-compute per-sheet table groupings: for each Quantbook
   413	    // sheet index, the table ids anchored there. Used to emit
   414	    // `<tableParts>` in the worksheet xml + rels.
   415	    let mut tables_by_sheet: std::collections::HashMap<usize, Vec<&TableExport>> =
   416	        std::collections::HashMap::new();
   417	    for t in tables {
   418	        tables_by_sheet.entry(t.sheet_idx).or_default().push(t);
   419	    }
   420	
   421	    let bytes = std::fs::read(path)?;
   422	    let mut reader =
   423	        zip::ZipArchive::new(std::io::Cursor::new(bytes.as_slice())).map_err(XlsxError::Zip)?;
   424	    let mut out_buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
   425	    let mut existing_names: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
   426	    {
   427	        let mut writer = zip::ZipWriter::new(std::io::Cursor::new(&mut out_buf));
   428	        for i in 0..reader.len() {
   429	            let mut entry = reader.by_index(i).map_err(XlsxError::Zip)?;
   430	            let name = entry.name().to_string();
   431	            existing_names.insert(name.clone());
   432	            let mut content = Vec::new();
   433	            entry.read_to_end(&mut content)?;
   434	            if name == "xl/workbook.xml" {
   435	                if inject_date1904 {
   436	                    content = inject_date1904_into_workbook_xml(content)?;
   437	                }
   438	                if !defined_names.is_empty() {
   439	                    content = inject_defined_names_into_workbook_xml(content, defined_names)?;
   440	                }
   441	            } else if name == "xl/styles.xml" {
   442	                if !custom_formats.is_empty() {
   443	                    content = inject_custom_formats_into_styles_xml(content, custom_formats)?;
   444	                }
   445	                if !cellxfs_roster.is_empty() {
   446	                    content = inject_cell_xfs_into_styles_xml(content, cellxfs_roster)?;
   447	                }
   448	            } else if name == "[Content_Types].xml" && !tables.is_empty() {
   449	                content = inject_table_overrides_into_content_types(content, tables)?;
   450	            } else if let Some(sheet_idx) = sheet_index_from_path(&name) {
   451	                if let Some(fixes) = sheet_fixes.get(sheet_idx) {
   452	                    if !fixes.is_empty() {
   453	                        content = apply_cell_fixes_to_sheet_xml(content, fixes)?;
   454	                    }
   455	                }
   456	                if let Some(sheet_tables) = tables_by_sheet.get(&sheet_idx) {
   457	                    content = inject_table_parts_into_sheet_xml(content, sheet_tables)?;
   458	                }
   459	            } else if let Some(sheet_idx) = sheet_rels_index_from_path(&name) {
   460	                if let Some(sheet_tables) = tables_by_sheet.get(&sheet_idx) {
   461	                    content = inject_table_rels(content, sheet_tables)?;
   462	                }
   463	            }
   464	            let opts = zip::write::FileOptions::default()
   465	                .compression_method(zip::CompressionMethod::Deflated);
   466	            writer.start_file(name, opts).map_err(XlsxError::Zip)?;
   467	            writer.write_all(&content)?;
   468	        }
   469	
   470	        // **W5-D-14.2 HIGH-3 closure:** emit new xl/tables/table{N}.xml
   860	
   861	    Err(XlsxError::Export(
   862	        "workbook.xml missing <workbook> root element".to_string(),
   863	    ))
   864	}

   866	/// Convert `xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet5.xml.rels` → `Some(4)` (0-indexed N-1).
   867	fn sheet_rels_index_from_path(name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
   868	    let stripped = name.strip_prefix("xl/worksheets/_rels/sheet")?;
   869	    let n_str = stripped.strip_suffix(".xml.rels")?;
   870	    n_str.parse::<usize>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_sub(1))
   871	}
   872	
   873	/// **W5-D-14.2 HIGH-5 closure:** inject `<numFmts>` into styles.xml.
   874	/// umya 2.2.0 does NOT write `<numFmts>` for cells without applied
   875	/// styles, so custom format codes registered in Quantbook's FormatTable
   876	/// (id >= 164) are silently dropped on export. We patch styles.xml
   877	/// post-write to add them as the FIRST child of `<styleSheet>`
   878	/// (OOXML requires `<numFmts>` before `<fonts>`).
   879	///
   880	/// If styles.xml doesn't exist (very unlikely from umya), creates a
   881	/// minimal one — but this path is exercised only as a defensive
   882	/// fallback; the real generated styles.xml always contains the
   883	/// scaffolding.
   884	fn inject_custom_formats_into_styles_xml(
   885	    content: Vec<u8>,
   886	    custom_formats: &[(u32, String)],
   887	) -> Result<Vec<u8>, XlsxError> {
   888	    let text = String::from_utf8(content)
   889	        .map_err(|e| XlsxError::Export(format!("styles.xml is not valid UTF-8: {e}")))?;
   890	
   891	    let mut numfmts = String::with_capacity(64 * custom_formats.len());
   892	    numfmts.push_str(&format!(r#"<numFmts count="{}">"#, custom_formats.len()));
   893	    for (id, code) in custom_formats {
   894	        numfmts.push_str(&format!(
   895	            r#"<numFmt numFmtId="{}" formatCode="{}"/>"#,
   896	            id,
   897	            xml_attr_escape(code),
   898	        ));
   899	    }
   900	    numfmts.push_str("</numFmts>");
   901	
   902	    // Case 1: existing <numFmts> — replace it entirely. (Unlikely
   903	    // since umya doesn't emit any, but handle defensively.)
   904	    //
   905	    // **W5-D-14.2.3 (separate-Opus M-1 closure):** check the
   906	    // non-self-closing `</numFmts>` form FIRST. The self-close `/>`
   907	    // search runs over the FULL remainder of the document, so if
   908	    // `<numFmts>` has self-closing children (`<numFmt ../>`), the
   909	    // `find("/>")` would match the CHILD's `/>` and truncate at the
   910	    // wrong place. Closing-tag form lets us cleanly bracket the
   911	    // outer element.
   912	    if let Some(start) = text.find("<numFmts") {
   913	        let after = start + "<numFmts".len();
   914	        if let Some(close_rel) = text[after..].find("</numFmts>") {
   915	            let end = after + close_rel + "</numFmts>".len();
   916	            let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + numfmts.len());
   917	            out.push_str(&text[..start]);
   918	            out.push_str(&numfmts);
   919	            out.push_str(&text[end..]);
   920	            return Ok(out.into_bytes());
   921	        }
   922	        // Truly self-closing `<numFmts ... />` form: find the FIRST
   923	        // `>` after the tag name and require the preceding byte to be
   924	        // `/`. That bounds the search to the actual element close.
   925	        if let Some(gt_rel) = text[after..].find('>') {
   926	            let end = after + gt_rel + 1;
   927	            if text[after..end].ends_with("/>") {
   928	                let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + numfmts.len());
   929	                out.push_str(&text[..start]);
   930	                out.push_str(&numfmts);
   931	                out.push_str(&text[end..]);
   932	                return Ok(out.into_bytes());
   933	            }
   934	        }
   935	    }
   936	
   937	    // Case 2: insert after the <styleSheet ...> opening tag.
   938	    if let Some(opening) = text.find("<styleSheet") {
   939	        let end_of_opening = text[opening..]
   940	            .find('>')
   941	            .map(|i| opening + i + 1)
   942	            .ok_or_else(|| {
   943	                XlsxError::Export("styles.xml has malformed <styleSheet>".to_string())
   944	            })?;
   945	        let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + numfmts.len());
   946	        out.push_str(&text[..end_of_opening]);
   947	        out.push_str(&numfmts);
   948	        out.push_str(&text[end_of_opening..]);
   949	        return Ok(out.into_bytes());
   950	    }
   951	
   952	    Err(XlsxError::Export(
   953	        "styles.xml missing <styleSheet> root element".to_string(),
   954	    ))
   955	}
   956	
   957	/// **W5-D-15 (XLSX-4-03 per-cell format closure):** replace umya's
   958	/// default `<cellXfs>` block with one that enumerates every FormatId
   959	/// referenced by any cell. Slot 0 is the default xf (numFmtId=0, no
   960	/// applyNumberFormat); slots 1..N follow the `cellxfs_roster` order
   961	/// (which matches the `xf_index` values minted at the cell-fix
   962	/// collection site so `<c s="N">` round-trips correctly).
   963	fn inject_cell_xfs_into_styles_xml(
   964	    content: Vec<u8>,
   965	    cellxfs_roster: &[FormatId],
   966	) -> Result<Vec<u8>, XlsxError> {
   967	    let text = String::from_utf8(content)
   968	        .map_err(|e| XlsxError::Export(format!("styles.xml is not valid UTF-8: {e}")))?;
   969	
   970	    let count = cellxfs_roster.len() + 1;
   971	    let mut block = String::with_capacity(64 * count);
   972	    block.push_str(&format!(r#"<cellXfs count="{}">"#, count));
   973	    // Slot 0: default xf.
   974	    block.push_str(r#"<xf numFmtId="0" fontId="0" fillId="0" borderId="0" xfId="0"/>"#);
   975	    for fid in cellxfs_roster {
   976	        block.push_str(&format!(
   977	            concat!(
   978	                r#"<xf numFmtId="{}" fontId="0" fillId="0" borderId="0" xfId="0" "#,
   979	                r#"applyNumberFormat="1"/>"#,
   980	            ),
   981	            fid.0,
   982	        ));
   983	    }
   984	    block.push_str("</cellXfs>");
   985	
   986	    // Case 1: existing <cellXfs> — replace. Closing-tag form first.
   987	    if let Some(start) = text.find("<cellXfs") {
   988	        let after = start + "<cellXfs".len();
   989	        if let Some(close_rel) = text[after..].find("</cellXfs>") {
   990	            let end = after + close_rel + "</cellXfs>".len();
   991	            let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + block.len());
   992	            out.push_str(&text[..start]);
   993	            out.push_str(&block);
   994	            out.push_str(&text[end..]);
   995	            return Ok(out.into_bytes());
   996	        }
   997	        if let Some(gt_rel) = text[after..].find('>') {
   998	            let end = after + gt_rel + 1;
   999	            if text[after..end].ends_with("/>") {
  1000	                let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + block.len());
  1001	                out.push_str(&text[..start]);
  1002	                out.push_str(&block);
  1003	                out.push_str(&text[end..]);
  1004	                return Ok(out.into_bytes());
  1005	            }
  1006	        }
  1007	    }
  1008	
  1009	    // Case 2: no existing <cellXfs> — insert at the end of styleSheet
  1010	    // (before </styleSheet>). umya always emits a cellXfs block so
  1011	    // this path is defensive only.
  1012	    if let Some(idx) = text.rfind("</styleSheet>") {
  1013	        let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + block.len());
  1014	        out.push_str(&text[..idx]);
  1015	        out.push_str(&block);
  1016	        out.push_str(&text[idx..]);
  1017	        return Ok(out.into_bytes());
  1018	    }

     1	//! Replay an `OpLog` against a `Workbook`.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): single entry point `replay_into(&OpLog, &mut
     4	//! Workbook, &FunctionRegistry) -> Result<usize, ReplayError>`. Returns the
     5	//! count of ops successfully applied; on failure, returns
     6	//! `ReplayError::At { index, kind }` carrying the position of the failing
     7	//! op and the underlying failure. The workbook is left in a partial state
     8	//! on failure (callers decide whether to discard, recover, or recompute).
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Replay semantics
    11	//!
    12	//! Each `Op` variant maps to one `Workbook` mutation:
    13	//!
    14	//! - `PutValue` → `Workbook::put_at` (after row/col bounds check).
    15	//! - `PutFormula` → `Workbook::put_formula` (text only; replay does NOT
    16	//!   re-evaluate — that's a separate step the caller drives via
    17	//!   `WorkbookRuntime::recompute_all`).
    18	//! - `ClearFormula` → `Workbook::clear_formula`.
    19	//! - `SetName` → `Workbook::set_name`. Reserved names (e.g. `AI`) surface
    20	//!   as `ReplayError::NameRejected`.
    21	//! - `AddSheet` → `Workbook::add_sheet_with_chunk_rows`.
    22	//! - `BatchCommit` → recurse on each inner op. Index reporting flattens:
    23	//!   a failure inside a BatchCommit reports the inner op's overall
    24	//!   position (current outer index + offset).
    25	//!
    26	//! ## Idempotence
    27	//!
    28	//! `replay_into` is idempotent only in the trivial sense: replaying twice
    29	//! against the same starting workbook produces the same final state IFF
    30	//! the underlying mutation methods are themselves idempotent (and they
    31	//! are — `put_at` / `put_formula` / `clear_formula` / `set_name` /
    32	//! `add_sheet` all are). Callers wanting at-most-once semantics across
    33	//! sessions track replay state themselves (Phase 5+ work).
    34	//!
    35	//! ## `registry` parameter
    36	//!
    37	//! Passed for API symmetry with `WorkbookRuntime::new(&mut wb, &registry)`.
    38	//! 2A.3.a's replay doesn't use it (formula evaluation is deferred to a
    39	//! separate `recompute_all` call), but keeping the parameter stable here
    40	//! avoids a breaking signature change in 2A.3.b/c when the eval path
    41	//! could land inside replay.

     1	//! `ql-oplog` — Loro-backed operation log for the Quantbook engine.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): scaffolding. Per Round 7 architectural lock
     4	//! T1-D05, Loro is reserved for the op log layer only — no other crate
     5	//! depends on it. CRDT semantics (inter-peer merge) are reserved for Phase
     6	//! 5+ multi-user work; Phase 2A.3 uses Loro as the persistence + future-
     7	//! CRDT-merge substrate.
     8	//!
     9	//! ## Surface
    10	//!
    11	//! - [`Op`] — the engine's mutation vocabulary (one variant per recordable
    12	//!   Workbook mutation).
    13	//! - [`OpLog`] — append-only log with `append`, `iter`, `len`, `is_empty`,
    14	//!   `export_bytes`, `import_bytes`.
    15	//! - [`replay_into`] — applies a log against a [`ql_storage::Workbook`].
    16	//! - [`OpLogError`], [`ReplayError`] — error surfaces (thiserror-derived).
    17	//!
    18	//! ## Scope
    19	//!
    20	//! 2A.3.a (2026-05-12) shipped the crate itself + tests. 2A.3.b wired
    21	//! `WorkbookRuntime` / `WorkbookTransaction` to emit ops. 2A.3.c (this
    22	//! commit) adds `oplog.bin` persistence alongside the `.qbook/` envelope
    23	//! via [`persistence::save_workbook_with_oplog`] /
    24	//! [`persistence::load_workbook_with_oplog`].
    25	//!
    26	//! # Stability
    27	//!
    28	//! Pre-0.2.0 the public API surface is in flux. `Op` carries
    29	//! `#[non_exhaustive]` because Phase 5 (CRDT collaboration) will
    30	//! add new op variants for sheet-scoped names, table mutations,
    31	//! presence, and undo grouping — downstream replayers must include
    32	//! a `_` arm. Error enums (`OpLogError`, `PersistenceError`,
    33	//! `ReplayError`, `FormatRejectedSource`) also carry the marker.
    34	//! Wire enums (`ReferenceModeWire`, `LocaleWire`) are exhaustive by
    35	//! design; variant additions are MAJOR-version events because the
    36	//! wire format and producer/replay sites are updated in lockstep.
    37	
    38	pub mod error;
    39	pub mod log;
    40	pub mod op;
    41	pub mod replay;
    42	pub mod wire;
    43	
    44	pub use error::OpLogError;
    45	pub use log::{OpLog, PRESENCE_COMMIT_ORIGIN};
    46	pub use op::{LocaleWire, Op, ReferenceModeWire};
    47	pub use replay::{replay_into, ReplayError};
    48	pub use wire::{CellWireValue, NamedTargetWire, WireDecodeError};
    49	
    50	// **Tier D2 (2026-05-19) — Phase 4.12 Opus-C HIGH-3 closure**: the
    51	// `persistence` module (save_workbook_with_oplog / load_workbook_with_oplog
    52	// / PersistenceError) moved to `ql-io::oplog_persistence`. The move

    21	/// Per-peer collaboration identifier.
    22	///
    23	/// Wraps a `u64` to match Loro's native peer-id type. Stable for
    24	/// the lifetime of a `CollabSession`; the user-facing tooling
    25	/// decides assignment policy. Two concurrent peers MUST have
    26	/// distinct ids — duplicate peer ids corrupt the document via
    27	/// conflicting OpIDs (Loro pitfall, surfaced by Phase 5.1 audit
    28	/// then closed by Phase 5.2.b wiring). Prefer per-process-random
    29	/// allocation unless your server enforces uniqueness explicitly.
    30	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Hash, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd)]
    31	pub struct PeerId(pub u64);
    32	
    33	impl PeerId {
    34	    /// Construct a `PeerId` from the raw u64.
    35	    pub const fn new(id: u64) -> Self {
    36	        Self(id)
    37	    }
    38	
    39	    /// Unwrap to the raw `u64`. Used at the Loro boundary
    40	    /// (`LoroDoc::set_peer_id` takes `u64`).
    41	    pub const fn as_u64(self) -> u64 {
    42	        self.0
    43	    }
    44	}

    47	    fn from(id: u64) -> Self {

    49	    }

    55	    }

    59	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:11:The single most serious finding: **`HIGH-001` — three of the four newly-added e2e tests are FAILING in the working tree** (`e2e_subtotal_sum_range_dispatch`, `e2e_subtotal_average_range_dispatch`, `e2e_subtotal_109_equivalent_to_sum_range`). They were labelled "W5-D-12.1 Codex HIGH-001 closure" in their comments, but the underlying closure is **incomplete** — adding `"SUBTOTAL"` to `is_aggregate_function` is necessary but NOT sufficient. Literal `Expr::RangeRef` is rejected by the binder unconditionally outside `BindContext::ReferenceArg`, including in `BindContext::AggregateArg`. The author was aware of this limitation (workbook_runtime.rs line 11875 explicitly notes `"Literal SUM(A1:A3) over a Range needs aggregate-arg binding which v1 routes via named ranges only"`), yet committed tests that exercise exactly the unsupported path. As a result `cargo test --workspace` fails — this is not a fly-by issue.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3009:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1515:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10204:A1. Correct. `loro::LoroDoc::set_peer_id` is only a wrapper over the internal doc setter: [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:985). The internal state doc says it changes the peer id “for the future txn”: [state.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/state.rs:491). Existing committed ops are not traversed or rewritten. Transaction creation captures the current peer at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:350), and commit writes `ID::new(self.peer, ...)` at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:448).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3010:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1516:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10208:A3. Safe after import. Loro `import` runs through `with_barrier`: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:568), snapshot decode requires an empty op log: [fast_snapshot.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/encoding/fast_snapshot.rs:145), and `set_peer_id` then updates only the current/future peer state.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3011:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1517:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10210:A4. Through `OpLog`, there is no public interleaving point between `list.push` and `doc.commit()` because `append` holds `&mut self`: [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:76). At raw Loro level, changing peer id during an auto-commit txn triggers a barrier: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:187). Pending txn ops keep the peer captured when that txn was created; future txn/appends use the new peer.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3013:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1522:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10263:A1. Correct. `loro::LoroDoc::set_peer_id` is only a wrapper over the internal doc setter: [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:985). The internal state doc says it changes the peer id “for the future txn”: [state.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/state.rs:491). Existing committed ops are not traversed or rewritten. Transaction creation captures the current peer at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:350), and commit writes `ID::new(self.peer, ...)` at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:448).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3014:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1523:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10267:A3. Safe after import. Loro `import` runs through `with_barrier`: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:568), snapshot decode requires an empty op log: [fast_snapshot.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/encoding/fast_snapshot.rs:145), and `set_peer_id` then updates only the current/future peer state.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3015:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1524:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10269:A4. Through `OpLog`, there is no public interleaving point between `list.push` and `doc.commit()` because `append` holds `&mut self`: [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:76). At raw Loro level, changing peer id during an auto-commit txn triggers a barrier: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:187). Pending txn ops keep the peer captured when that txn was created; future txn/appends use the new peer.

Current `OpLog::append` commits immediately in [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:84), so no current in-flight ops are left to be swept up, but future batching would be coupled unless documented.

Yes: `doc.commit()` commits the cumulative pending transaction for the whole doc, not just presence. Loro says “Commit the cumulative auto commit transaction” and every operation has a transaction in [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:575). Current `OpLog::append` commits immediately in [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:84), so no current in-flight ops are left to be swept up, but future batching would be coupled unless documented.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:5470:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10204:A1. Correct. `loro::LoroDoc::set_peer_id` is only a wrapper over the internal doc setter: [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:985). The internal state doc says it changes the peer id “for the future txn”: [state.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/state.rs:491). Existing committed ops are not traversed or rewritten. Transaction creation captures the current peer at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:350), and commit writes `ID::new(self.peer, ...)` at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:448).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:5471:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10208:A3. Safe after import. Loro `import` runs through `with_barrier`: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:568), snapshot decode requires an empty op log: [fast_snapshot.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/encoding/fast_snapshot.rs:145), and `set_peer_id` then updates only the current/future peer state.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:5472:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10210:A4. Through `OpLog`, there is no public interleaving point between `list.push` and `doc.commit()` because `append` holds `&mut self`: [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:76). At raw Loro level, changing peer id during an auto-commit txn triggers a barrier: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:187). Pending txn ops keep the peer captured when that txn was created; future txn/appends use the new peer.

     1	# Audit protocol — Quantbook engine
     2	
     3	**Status:** MANDATORY for every Claude Code window working on the Quantbook engine.
     4	**Established:** 2026-05-13 (W5-59 finalization session).
     5	**Companion:** `docs/audits/2026-05-13-engine-session-final-handoff.md` (current handoff). Read that FIRST, then this.
     6	
     7	This is the operating manual. Every rule below is either **MANDATORY**, **RECOMMENDED**, or **FORBIDDEN**. Use Codex (and where indicated, a Sonnet agent in parallel) per the cadence specified — the W5-52 mega-audit pattern caught a real HIGH bug that single-auditor review would not have found.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Purpose
    12	
    13	Lock down the practices that keep the engine shipping correct, honest, auditable code across sessions. The biggest risk is silent doc/code divergence becoming the next window's starting premise — that already almost happened in W5-50 (`on_clear_formula` clear-path bug shipped under "GAP-G-01 closed" framing; caught only by the W5-52 parallel mega-audit). This protocol prevents that.
    14	
    15	---
    16	
    17	## Cycle discipline (CLAUDE.md alignment)
    18	
    19	- **MANDATORY ≤2 plan-implement-audit cycles per session.** A cycle is: design + implement + verify. If you're hitting cycle 3, STOP and write a handoff for a fresh session.
    20	- **MANDATORY pause-for-context-reset at ~60% context budget.** Recommend fresh session at >60%; strongly recommend at >80%.
    21	- **The W5-49 → W5-58 session ran past this limit** under explicit user direction. The user is responsible for that override — DO NOT do it on your own.
    22	
    23	---
    24	
    25	## Per-commit gates (MANDATORY — all 7 green at every shippable commit)
    26	
    27	Run these as a strict block before any commit. If any fail, fix and re-run.
    28	
    29	```bash
    30	# 1. fmt
    31	mac zsh -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; \
    32	  cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine && \
    33	  cargo fmt --all -- --check'
    34	
    35	# 2. clippy with -D warnings (workspace + all targets)
    36	mac zsh -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; \
    37	  cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine && \
    38	  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings'
    39	
    40	# 3. workspace tests (verify count vs the latest baseline)
    41	mac zsh -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; \
    42	  cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine && \
    43	  cargo test --locked --workspace 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result:" | \
    44	  awk "/ok\. [0-9]+ passed/ {sum+=\$4} END {print sum}"'
    45	
    46	# 4. build-flags guard (catches -Ctarget-cpu=native sneaking in)
    47	bash /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/scripts/check-build-flags.sh
    48	
    49	# 5. cargo-lock pin guard (18 watched packages must stay aligned)
    50	bash /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/scripts/check-cargo-lock-pins.sh
    51	
    52	# 6. multiversion clones (Mac-side disassembly check)
    53	mac zsh -lc 'bash /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/scripts/check-multiversion-clones.sh'
    54	
    55	# 7. cargo audit (1 pre-existing allowed warning OK: atomic-polyfill)
    56	mac zsh -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; \
    57	  cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine && \
    58	  cargo audit'
    59	```
    60	
    61	**FORBIDDEN:**
    62	- Committing without all 7 gates green.
    63	- Bypassing gates with `--no-verify` (the pre-commit husky hook). If a hook fails, fix the underlying cause.
    64	- Claiming "all gates green" in a commit message without actually running them.
    65	
    66	**RECOMMENDED:**
    67	- Run a targeted `cargo test -p <crate> --lib <pattern>` first when iterating; full workspace last.
    68	- After `docs/compat/excel-matrix.md` edits, run `scripts/report-compat-coverage.sh` to confirm coverage number is honest.
    69	- Before `git commit`, run `git diff --check` for whitespace errors.
    70	
    71	---
    72	
    73	## Per-phase mega-audit (MANDATORY — the W5-52 pattern)
    74	
    75	After every phase completion OR substantial run (e.g. ≥3 commits in one feature area), dispatch **TWO independent auditors in parallel**: Codex and a Sonnet agent. Why both: the W5-52 audit found a HIGH bug because both auditors independently flagged it — single-auditor review would not have given the same confidence.
    76	
    77	### Auditor brief template
    78	
    79	The brief MUST include:
    80	1. **Context** — branch state, HEAD, commits to audit (shas), test count, gate status
    81	2. **Required reading** — exact file paths (docs + code) the auditor must read
    82	3. **Session ledger** — commit-by-commit summary
    83	4. **Specific concerns** — what to challenge (don't just ask "is it correct"; ask 6-8 concrete questions, like the W5-49 review brief did)
    84	5. **What to report** — HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW + test gaps + verdict
    85	
    86	Save brief at `docs/audits/<date>-<scope>-megaudit-prompt.md`.
    87	
    88	### Codex dispatch
    89	
    90	```bash
   180	[ ] Read docs/known-gaps.md (open + recently closed gaps)
   181	[ ] cd to repo root, git status -uno (clean expected), git log --oneline -15
   182	[ ] Run cargo test --workspace via mac bridge — confirm baseline test count
   183	[ ] Run the 7 gates per § Per-commit gates — confirm clean state
   184	[ ] Decide work mode (per-handoff-recommendation or user-requested)
   185	```
   186	
   187	**FORBIDDEN:** starting code work without all 9 items above completed.
   188	
   189	---
   190	
   191	## Critical gotchas — sharp edges the next window must know
   192	
   193	These are bugs that have actually tripped me up. Read them before any work.
   194	
   195	### 1. OrbStack mac bridge — cargo PATH
   196	
   197	`cargo` is NOT on the default PATH inside the OrbStack Linux VM. EVERY cargo command must go through:
   198	
   199	```bash
   200	mac zsh -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; \
   201	  cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine && \
   202	  cargo <subcommand> [args]'
   203	```
   204	
   205	A direct `cargo test --workspace` from inside the VM SILENTLY produces no output (it can't find `cargo`).
   206	
   207	### 2. VM `/tmp` ≠ Mac `/tmp`
   208	
   209	When dispatching Codex via `mac zsh -lc 'codex exec ...'`, the prompt and output files MUST live under `/Users/sanzhar/...` (shared filesystem). `/tmp/anything` is invisible across the boundary. Examples:
   210	- BAD: prompt at `/tmp/audit-prompt.md`
   340	
   341	# 2. Branch + state check
   342	cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook
   343	git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD   # expect: feat/quantbook-engine
   344	git log --oneline -5
   345	git status --short
   346	
   347	# 3. Test count check
   348	mac zsh -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; \
   349	  cd /Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine && \
   350	  cargo test --workspace 2>&1 | grep "test result:" | \
   351	  python3 -c "
   352	import sys, re
   353	passed = failed = 0
   354	for line in sys.stdin:
   355	    m = re.search(r'(\d+) passed.*?(\d+) failed', line)
   356	    if m: passed += int(m.group(1)); failed += int(m.group(2))
   357	print(f'PASSED: {passed}, FAILED: {failed}')"'
   358	
   359	# 4. Has any code been changed without a 7-gate pass? Look at staged + unstaged diff.
   360	git diff --stat
   361	git diff --cached --stat
   362	
   363	# 5. Cycle-discipline self-check
   364	# Count plan-implement-audit cycles in this session. If > 2, you should be writing a handoff for a fresh session, NOT continuing.
   365	```
   366	
   367	### Recovery — "what to do if you violated the protocol"
   368	
   369	**If you skipped a per-commit gate and already committed:**
   370	1. Run the missed gate now.
   371	2. If it passes — note the gap in the next commit message (NOT silently); add a `Gate skipped in <prior_commit>; re-run clean here` line.
   372	3. If it fails — IMMEDIATELY write the fix. Do NOT push. The commit must NOT be the user's first encounter with the failure.
   373	
   374	**If you skipped a per-phase mega-audit and the work is shippable-state:**
   375	1. Run the audit retroactively before declaring the phase closed.
   376	2. If findings emerge, file them with the original phase's number (e.g. `W5-NN audit closure addresses W5-MM phase audit findings`).
   377	3. If the phase is already labeled "closed" in docs, mark it `⚠️ AUDIT-RETRO-PENDING` until the audit runs.
   378	
   379	**If you ran > 2 plan-implement-audit cycles in one session without user override:**
   380	1. STOP. Don't start cycle 4.
   381	2. Write a handoff covering everything done in cycles 1-3.
   382	3. Commit the work-in-progress (or stash with notes) and explicitly tell the user the session is over.
   383	
   384	**If you discovered the previous session left stale docs (date, HEAD, test count drift):**
   385	1. DON'T trust the docs over the code. Run the actual command (`git rev-parse HEAD`, `cargo test --workspace`) and pin reality.
   386	2. Add a doc-drift fix to the next commit; reference the prior session.
   387	3. Update `MEMORY.md` / `current_work.md` only AFTER verifying the new state.
   388	
   389	**If Codex disagrees with you and you don't understand why:**
   390	1. Re-read Codex's full output, including the parts after "summary".

     1	//! `ql-collab` — Phase 5 multi-user CRDT collaboration crate.
     2	//!
     3	//! **Phase 5.2.a (2026-05-19, scaffold ship):** establishes the
     4	//! module shape per the audit-closed design at
     5	//! `docs/architecture/crdt-data-model.md`. Phase 5.1 locked Option
     6	//! A (preserve op-log shape on top of Loro `LoroList`); this crate
     7	//! is the layer above ql-oplog that orchestrates multi-peer
     8	//! collaboration.
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Module layout
    11	//!
    12	//! - [`peer`] — `PeerId` type. Stable per-session identifier used
    13	//!   to attribute ops + presence state. Wraps Loro's `u64` peer id.
    14	//! - [`session`] — `CollabSession`: per-peer state holder that
    15	//!   wraps an `OpLog`, manages local appends, and exposes
    16	//!   `merge_bytes` + `export_bytes` for transport integration.
    17	//! - [`transport`] — `Transport` trait + 2 impls: `NoopTransport`
    18	//!   (test stub) and `LoopbackTransport` (Phase 5.5 V1 ship
    19	//!   2026-05-19 — in-process paired endpoints for 2-peer
    20	//!   round-trip tests). Phase 5.5 V2 V1 (2026-05-19, `ffd8f6e5f05`)
    21	//!   added `CollabSession` typed transport methods
    22	//!   (attach/detach/flush/poll). Phase 5.5 V2 V2 / V3 pending —
    23	//!   auto-flush + version-vector deltas + WebSocket impl.
    24	//! - [`presence`] — per-peer ephemeral cursor + selection state
    25	//!   (Phase 5.6 V1 ship 2026-05-19). `PresenceState` JSON-encoded
    26	//!   into the shared `LoroDoc`'s `"presence"` LoroMap (LWW per key).
    27	//! - [`undo`] — peer-local undo/redo via Loro's `UndoManager`.
    28	//!   V1 ship 2026-05-19 (`89c02b9d83e`): 7 undo/redo methods.
    29	//!   V2 V1 (`6138a7203f6` + `e199a5fda5a`): atomic grouping +
    30	//!   merge-interval. V2 V1.1: RAII `start_undo_group_scoped`
    31	//!   returning `UndoGroupGuard`. V2 V2 pending — push/pop
    32	//!   listeners.
    33	//!
    34	//! ## Stability

    36	//! Pre-0.2.0: the public API is in flux. Phase 5.2.b through 5.7
